findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain an authorization server containing only the Users resource and its scopes; they never receive the Clients all-resource or the new configure/map-role scopes. Creating a Client permission in such a realm will fail when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find the new scopes, and global Client permission evaluation can encounter a missing all-Clients resource. Initialization must reconcile and add missing schema scopes/resources for existing clients rather than treating their presence as proof that the schema is current.

findings.title: A realm-wide Clients/manage grant does not grant global view or list access
findings.body: `canManage()` recognizes a V2 all-Clients `manage` permission, but `canView()` checks only the legacy default roles and the V2 `view` permission. As a result, an administrator granted only all-Clients `manage` can manage a specific client through `canManage(client)`, but fails global view/list checks (`canList()` is defined in terms of `canView()`). This contradicts the per-client path, where manage/configure implies view, and prevents the expected list/view behavior after granting the all-Clients manage scope. Include the manage implication in the global view decision.

findings.title: Role-mapping checks no longer honor manage permission
findings.body: The three role-mapping methods at lines 92, 97, and 102 only test their exact V2 map scope. They bypass `canManage(client)`, unlike configure/view, so both the established `manage-clients` admin role and a V2 Clients/manage grant lose the ability to map client roles, map composites, or map client-scope roles. Existing administrators that could perform these operations are consequently rejected with 403 when V2 is enabled. These checks need to preserve the manage implication before testing their dedicated scopes.

findings.title: Client-resource cleanup is disabled for V2-only deployments
findings.body: The client-removal listener is now guarded by the legacy `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature flag, while V2 evaluation is selected by the independent `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` flag. In a V2-only deployment, deleting a client no longer invokes any cleanup for the per-client authorization resource created by this change, leaving its resource and policies orphaned in the admin-permissions resource server. Conversely, if both flags are enabled, the listener calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. V2 needs its own client-removal cleanup path (or a compatible implementation) rather than suppressing the listener based on the legacy flag.
